canonical_senses.label: ghost, shade of the dead
canonical_senses.gloss: The breath-soul that leaves the body at the moment of death and survives in Hades as a shade; the dominant Homeric sense.
canonical_senses.period_notes: Dominant in Homer and in later literary imitations of Homer; largely displaced by 'soul, self' in Classical prose but retained in poetic and funerary contexts.

representative_evidence.evidence_quote: Many a brave soul did it send hurrying down to Hades (Butler, Il. 1.3)

canonical_senses.notes: Lattimore's preface note (reproduced in gold_note_relied_upon of candidate 1) is the philological anchor for this sense and was used to exclude 'soul, self' readings in Homeric passages even where a translator used the English word 'soul'.

canonical_senses.label: breath, life-force
canonical_senses.gloss: The breath or animating principle of a living body; the literal etymological sense, and the physiological aspect of the Homeric ψυχή before it has left the body.
canonical_senses.period_notes: Attested from Homer onward; the etymological sense ('to breathe', PIE *bʰes-) is visible throughout.

representative_evidence.evidence_quote: he gasped out his life (Butler, Il. 5.296)

canonical_senses.notes: Shares a fuzzy boundary with 'ghost, shade' — the Homeric ψυχή is continuous from 'breath in a living body' through 'breath-soul at the moment of death' to 'shade in Hades'. The three senses are separable but not neatly disjoint.

canonical_senses.label: soul, self
canonical_senses.gloss: The rational, animate soul of a living person; the seat of character, thought, and moral agency. The classical and post-classical dominant sense.
canonical_senses.period_notes: Becomes dominant in Classical philosophical prose (Socrates, Plato); present as the default sense in Hellenistic and Imperial Greek; continues into Koine with theological overlays.

representative_evidence.evidence_quote: take care of your soul (Jowett, Apology 29e)

canonical_senses.notes: Jowett's commentary on Apology 29e-30a is the key anchor. Candidate 6 (Matt. 6.25) overlaps with the newly proposed 'life' sense — see inventory_notes.

canonical_senses.label: life
canonical_senses.gloss: Life as the thing that can be saved or lost; distinctively Koine and especially common in the Septuagint and New Testament, where ψυχή functions as a near-equivalent of Hebrew נֶפֶשׁ.
canonical_senses.period_notes: Koine usage; overlaps with 'soul, self' in contexts where the referent is the whole living person.

representative_evidence.evidence_quote: take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat (Matt. 6.25)

canonical_senses.notes: Admitted as a candidate beyond the LSJ inventory structure because Koine usage is distinctive enough (and theologically loaded enough) that flattening it into 'soul, self' would obscure a real register shift. A stricter synthesis might treat it as a subsense of 'soul, self' with a Koine register tag.

senses_in_reference_but_unsupported.reference_sense: seat of thought and feeling (LSJ IV)
senses_in_reference_but_unsupported.reason: Not distinguishable from 'soul, self' in our demo corpus at current coverage; the subtler Platonic partition of ψυχή into rational/spirited/appetitive would require Republic IV and would pull the sense into a technical philosophical stratum.
Demo corpus does not include Phaedo or Plotinus; would require those sources to establish.

senses_beyond_reference.rationale: Koine usage (LXX / NT) is distinct enough to warrant its own label even though LSJ subsumes it under 'breath, life'. Flagged for reviewer attention.

inventory_notes: Four canonical senses with clear diachronic structure: Homeric 'ghost' + 'breath' → Classical 'soul, self' → Koine 'life / soul' with religious overlay. Gold note from Lattimore's preface was decisive for separating the Homeric senses from the Classical. Demo-corpus coverage is too thin to resolve the Platonic subdivisions (rational / spirited / appetitive); production expansion should add Republic IV and Phaedo to address this. Candidates from Antigone not yet included in this sample but would fall under 'soul, self' with a tragic register tag.
